quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn that construction work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other cars, pedestrians, and traffic signals. What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other cars, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams instead—they light up the road and objects better in fog.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains, cars, and bicyclists all share the road.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line on the road mean?

options.text: You can pass if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line means you can pass from your lane if it is safe. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Honk your horn to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: On slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with care.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet appears. These conditions make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the side of the road and empty.
When it approaches you, even if lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: When parked facing downhill, which way should the front wheels point?
questions.explanation: When parked facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or shoulder. If your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull over and let faster cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit if weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow centerlines mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What colors are the signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?
questions.explanation: Direction and destination signs are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way at which traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A solid green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never try to pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Get out and walk to the back of your car to check if it is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk to the back of your car to check if it is clear.
questions.explanation: Always look out your back window and mirrors when backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially with children nearby. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.

questions.question: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, check if it is safe, then pass the bus.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the red lights turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped until the red lights turn off.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended. Never try to pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers behind you about your blind spot.
Slow down to reduce your blind spot.
Check your mirrors, then look straight ahead.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and your blind spots. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
